name: Cynthia Kenyon

primary_works.title: A C. elegans mutant that lives twice as long as wild type (Nature)
daf-16/FOXO as the downstream effector of daf-2/IGF signalling

field_contribution: Showed that a single-gene mutation (daf-2, the worm insulin/IGF-1 receptor) doubles lifespan in C. elegans and that the effect requires the FOXO-family transcription factor daf-16. This converted aging from an unregulated wear-and-tear process into a genetically tractable, hormonally controlled program.
why_indexed: The first demonstration that aging rate is set by a discrete, conserved signalling pathway — the founding result of modern molecular gerontology.

name: Yoshinori Ohsumi

primary_works.title: Autophagy in yeast: visualization of autophagic bodies in vacuoles
Identification of the ATG genes

field_contribution: Used yeast vacuoles to visualize autophagy directly and then identified the core ATG genes that execute it, mapping the molecular machinery of how cells recycle their own components under starvation. Won the 2016 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
why_indexed: Defined the genetic machinery of autophagy, now one of the twelve hallmarks of aging and the mechanistic basis of fasting/mTOR-inhibition longevity claims.

name: Carlos López-Otín

primary_works.title: The Hallmarks of Aging (Cell, w/ Blasco, Partridge, Serrano, Kroemer)
Hallmarks of Aging: An expanding universe (12 hallmarks)

field_contribution: Lead author of the 2013 'Hallmarks of Aging' framework, which organized the aging literature into nine (later twelve) categorical hallmarks — genomic instability, telomere attrition, epigenetic alteration, loss of proteostasis, deregulated nutrient sensing, mitochondrial dysfunction, cellular senescence, stem-cell exhaustion, altered intercellular communication, plus disabled autophagy, dysbiosis, chronic inflammation.
why_indexed: Provides the consensus organizing ontology of mainstream geroscience — the spine onto which nearly every other figure in this map is hung.

name: Judith Campisi

primary_works.title: Senescent cells, tumor suppression, and organismal aging: the SASP
Cellular senescence: when bad things happen to good cells

field_contribution: Established that cellular senescence is antagonistically pleiotropic — tumor-suppressive early in life but pro-aging late — and characterized the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), the cocktail of inflammatory factors senescent cells secrete that drives tissue dysfunction and 'inflammaging'.
why_indexed: Turned senescence from a tissue-culture curiosity into a causal driver of aging and the rationale for the entire senolytics field.

name: Eric Verdin
region: Buck Institute for Research on Aging (president), USA

primary_works.title: NAD+ metabolism and the control of energy homeostasis (review)
Sirtuins and NAD+ in the aging immune system

field_contribution: Characterized how NAD+ decline with age impairs sirtuin and mitochondrial function and links metabolism to immune aging; as Buck president steers a major geroscience institute. Work centers on ketone bodies (beta-hydroxybutyrate) and NAD+ as signalling metabolites, not just energy substrates.
why_indexed: A leading voice on NAD+/sirtuin biology grounded in rigorous metabolism rather than supplement marketing — useful counterweight in the NAD+ conflict.

name: Matt Kaeberlein
region: formerly Univ. of Washington; Optispan, USA

primary_works.title: Rapamycin extends lifespan and healthspan (multiple)
The Dog Aging Project / TRIAD rapamycin trial

field_contribution: A leading translational advocate for rapamycin (mTOR inhibition) as the best-evidenced pharmacological geroprotector, and co-founder of the Dog Aging Project, which runs a randomized rapamycin trial in companion dogs as a bridge between mouse ITP data and human aging.
why_indexed: Bridges the strongest animal longevity signal (rapamycin) toward translation, and is an outspoken critic of weakly-evidenced longevity hype.

name: Nir Barzilai
region: Albert Einstein College of Medicine, USA

primary_works.title: Longevity genes in Ashkenazi Jewish centenarians (CETP, APOC3, IGF-1)
Metformin as a Tool to Target Aging (TAME trial design)

field_contribution: Identified longevity-associated gene variants (CETP, APOC3, growth-hormone/IGF-1 axis) in a cohort of centenarians, and designed the TAME (Targeting Aging with Metformin) trial — the first attempt to get a regulator (FDA) to accept aging itself as a trial endpoint.
why_indexed: Created the regulatory template for treating aging as an indication, and grounds it in human centenarian genetics rather than model organisms.

name: Valter Longo
region: USC Longevity Institute, USA / IFOM Milan

primary_works.title: Fasting-mimicking diet promotes regeneration and healthspan (Cell Metab)
The Longevity Diet (book)

field_contribution: Showed that periodic fasting and a calorie/protein-restricted 'fasting-mimicking diet' (FMD) lower IGF-1, trigger autophagy and stem-cell regeneration, and improve metabolic markers; commercialized the FMD as ProLon. A principal champion of the high-protein-shortens-lifespan side of the protein/mTOR conflict.
why_indexed: Translated fasting biology from yeast/mouse into a defined, tested human dietary protocol — and is a named party in the field's central protein conflict.
disputed: High-protein-is-harmful position is contested by Attia/Galpin (muscle, elderly mortality); likely age-dependent. Commercial ProLon stake is a COI.

name: Vadim Gladyshev
region: Brigham & Women's / Harvard Medical School, USA

primary_works.title: Molecular signatures of mammalian longevity (comparative transcriptomics)
Universal DNA methylation aging clock across mammals (w/ Horvath)

field_contribution: Uses cross-species comparison (from short-lived mice to long-lived naked mole-rats, whales, bats) to find molecular correlates of longevity, and co-built pan-mammalian epigenetic clocks. Also frames aging quantitatively via entropy/information loss and 'biological age' from multi-omics.
why_indexed: Brings comparative and information-theoretic rigor to what longevity actually selects for across mammals, not just one model organism.

name: Steve Horvath

primary_works.title: DNA methylation age of human tissues and cell types (the Horvath clock)
DNA methylation GrimAge predicts lifespan and healthspan

field_contribution: Built the first multi-tissue epigenetic clock — a weighted set of ~353 CpG methylation sites whose state predicts chronological age across nearly all human tissues — establishing DNAm age as a measurable biomarker of biological aging, later extended to mortality-predicting clocks (GrimAge).
why_indexed: Made 'biological age' a quantitative, reproducible measurement, the dependent variable nearly every intervention now tries to move.

name: Morgan Levine

primary_works.title: PhenoAge: an epigenetic biomarker of mortality (Aging)
DunedinPACE: a DNA methylation pace-of-aging (w/ Belsky)

field_contribution: Developed PhenoAge — a clock trained on clinical mortality rather than chronological age — and contributed to DunedinPACE, which measures the *rate* of aging from a single blood draw. Shifted clock-building from 'how old are your cells' to 'how fast are you aging and how likely to die'.
why_indexed: Reframed biological-age measurement around outcomes (mortality, healthspan), giving interventions a clinically meaningful target.

name: Tony Wyss-Coray

primary_works.title: Young blood reverses age-related impairments in cognitive function (Nat Med)
Organ aging signatures in plasma proteome predict mortality (Nature)

field_contribution: Showed that young-mouse plasma improves old-brain function via heterochronic parabiosis, and built plasma-proteomic 'organ clocks' that estimate the biological age of individual organs from blood proteins, revealing that organs age at different rates within one person.
why_indexed: Bridged young-blood rejuvenation biology to a measurable, organ-specific aging readout in humans.

name: Irina & Michael Conboy

primary_works.title: Rejuvenation of aged progenitor cells by exposure to a young systemic environment (Nature)
Notch/TGF-beta and the muscle stem-cell niche; small-blood-volume exchange

field_contribution: Demonstrated heterochronic parabiosis — joining old and young mouse circulations rejuvenates old muscle/liver stem cells via systemic factors (Notch, TGF-beta) — and later argued the effect is mostly *dilution of old pro-aging factors* rather than youthful factors, via neutral blood-exchange experiments.
why_indexed: The founding modern parabiosis result and the source of the 'old blood is the problem' reframing that drives plasma-dilution therapeutics.
disputed: Young-factors vs. old-factor-dilution interpretation is unresolved; GDF11 rejuvenation claims (Wagers) are contested.

name: Shinya Yamanaka

primary_works.title: Induction of pluripotent stem cells from fibroblasts by four factors (Cell)
Human iPS cells from adult fibroblasts

field_contribution: Showed that four transcription factors (Oct4, Sox2, Klf4, c-Myc — 'Yamanaka factors') can reprogram an adult somatic cell back to an embryonic-like pluripotent state, resetting its epigenetic and apparent biological age. Nobel Prize 2012.
why_indexed: Proved cellular age is reversible by epigenetic reprogramming — the mechanistic basis of the entire partial-reprogramming rejuvenation field (Altos, NewLimit).

name: Juan Carlos Izpisúa Belmonte
region: formerly Salk Institute; Altos Labs, USA/Spain

primary_works.title: In vivo amelioration of age-associated hallmarks by partial reprogramming (Cell)
Reprogramming to recover youthful epigenetic information (collaborations)

field_contribution: Demonstrated that cyclic, partial expression of Yamanaka factors in living mice reverses signs of aging in tissues without erasing cell identity or causing teratomas — establishing 'partial reprogramming' as an in-vivo rejuvenation strategy. A scientific lead at Altos Labs.
why_indexed: Translated reprogramming from a dish to a whole organism, the proof-of-concept for in-vivo age reversal.
disputed: Durability, safety, and cancer risk of in-vivo reprogramming remain open; some Salk-era papers drew scrutiny.

name: David Sinclair
tradition: sirtuin / NAD+ / information theory of aging

primary_works.title: Sirtuin activators (resveratrol) extend lifespan in yeast (Nature)
Lifespan: Why We Age and Why We Don't Have To (book)

field_contribution: Champion of the sirtuin/NAD+ axis of aging — resveratrol and NMN as sirtuin/NAD+ modulators — and of the 'information theory of aging,' which holds that aging is loss of epigenetic information, reversible by partial reprogramming. A prolific communicator and biotech founder.
why_indexed: The most prominent popularizer of the NAD+/sirtuin and epigenetic-reprogramming theses; indexed for influence, with claims flagged as contested.
disputed: Resveratrol/sirtuin mechanism (Sirtris, sold to GSK) heavily disputed; NMN human benefit unproven; 2024 'biological age reversal' and supplement claims drew strong criticism from peers (incl. Brenner, Kaeberlein).

name: Aubrey de Grey

primary_works.title: Ending Aging / SENS framework (book)
Robust Mouse Rejuvenation (RMR) program, LEV Foundation

field_contribution: Proposed SENS (Strategies for Engineered Negligible Senescence) — recasting aging as seven categories of accumulated molecular/cellular damage to be repaired rather than metabolism to be slowed — and 'longevity escape velocity.' Now runs the LEV Foundation's combination-therapy mouse rejuvenation trials.
why_indexed: Reframed the aging problem as a damage-repair engineering target, shaping how a generation of the longevity movement thinks; indexed for influence, claims contested.
disputed: Timeline predictions ('1000-year-olds') widely regarded as over-optimistic; SENS's seven-category sufficiency is unproven; non-traditional credentials and 2021 misconduct allegations (later partially addressed) are part of the record.

name: George Church
region: Harvard Medical School / Wyss Institute, USA

primary_works.title: Multiplex genome engineering using CRISPR (Science, w/ collaborators)
Gene-therapy combinations for aging reversal (mouse, w/ Rejuvenate Bio)

field_contribution: A founder of genomics (early sequencing methods, the Personal Genome Project) and synthetic biology, now applying multiplexed gene therapy to aging — e.g., combination AAV gene therapies (FGF21, TGFβ, αKlotho) that ameliorate multiple age-related diseases in mice via Rejuvenate Bio.
why_indexed: Brings genome-engineering scale to aging intervention and anchors the gene-therapy approach to longevity.

name: Martin Picard

primary_works.title: Mitochondrial functions modulate neuroendocrine, metabolic, inflammatory responses to stress (PNAS)
The energetic cost of allostasis and 'mitochondrial information processing'

field_contribution: Founded 'mitochondrial psychobiology' — showing mitochondria are not just power plants but signal-integrating organelles that translate psychosocial stress into cellular and physiological responses, with measurable energetic costs (allostatic load) and inter-mitochondrial communication.
why_indexed: Connects the biophysical substrate (mitochondria, bridging up to canon-05-biophysics) to stress, recovery, and aging — a key cross-domain node.
cross_branch_note: bridges UP to bucket-canon/05-biophysics (mitochondria); see Wallace, Nick Lane cards there

name: Peter Attia

primary_works.title: Outlive: The Science and Art of Longevity (book)
The Drive (podcast)

field_contribution: Synthesized a practice framework ('Medicine 3.0') centered on the four horsemen of chronic disease, the 'centenarian decathlon' (training backward from desired late-life function), aggressive lipid (ApoB) management, VO2max and strength as primary longevity levers, and detailed biomarker tracking. A translator/communicator, not a primary researcher.
why_indexed: The most influential synthesizer of mainstream longevity practice for clinicians and the public; indexed as translator — grade his cited primary sources, not his summaries.
disputed: Single contribution is synthesis/communication, not new evidence; champions high protein + strength against the Longo protein-restriction side.

name: Rhonda Patrick

primary_works.title: Sulforaphane / Nrf2 and broccoli-sprout work (PhD-era + reviews)
FoundMyFitness (podcast/site)

field_contribution: Communicates micronutrient and hormesis science to a broad audience — sulforaphane/Nrf2, omega-3 index, vitamin D, sauna (heat-shock proteins), and the 'micronutrient triage' theory (Ames). Trained in biochemistry; primarily a high-fidelity science communicator who reads and summarizes primary literature.
why_indexed: A leading bridge between nutrition/hormesis primary literature and the public; indexed as communicator.

name: Andrew Huberman
region: Stanford University; Huberman Lab podcast, USA

primary_works.title: Huberman Lab (podcast)
Retinal circuits / neural regeneration (primary academic work)

field_contribution: A vision-neuroscientist who became the dominant podcast communicator of behavioral 'protocols' — morning light for circadian entrainment, NSDR/yoga-nidra, deliberate cold/heat, breathing for state control. The protocols repackage existing literature; his role is communication and protocolization.
why_indexed: The most-consumed translator of circadian/light/breath/cold protocols to the public; indexed strictly as communicator — verify each protocol's primary source and effect size.
disputed: Protocol effect sizes are often overstated relative to the underlying evidence tier; mechanism-to-outcome leaps are common in the format.

name: Bryan Johnson

primary_works.title: Blueprint protocol (open-sourced diet/supplement/measurement stack)
Rejuvenation Olympics / open biomarker data

field_contribution: Runs the most extensively measured and fully open single-subject longevity experiment — a fixed diet, ~100-supplement stack, exercise, sleep, and dense biomarker/imaging panel ('Don't Die'), publishing all protocols and results. The contribution is the open, instrumented N=1 dataset itself, not validated efficacy.
why_indexed: The reference example of the practitioner-N=1 tier — maximal measurement, zero randomization; indexed as data, graded nequals1.
disputed: No causal inference possible from N=1; many interventions lack RCT support; commercial Blueprint products are a COI.

name: Jack Kruse

primary_works.title: Quantum biology / 'Time #' blog series (jackkruse.com)
Cold thermogenesis & 'leptin reset' protocols

field_contribution: An independent neurosurgeon who built a heterodox synthesis arguing that mitochondrial function is governed by light (UV/IR/red), magnetism/EMF, water structure, and deuterium — and that circadian-light mismatch and non-native EMF are root causes of modern disease. Protocols: morning sun, cold thermogenesis, blue-light avoidance, 'leptin reset'.
why_indexed: The central practitioner node connecting circadian/light/cold to the biophysics substrate; one partial source for the 05-biophysics branch. Indexed fringe-to-canon — mechanism claims mostly speculative tier.
cross_branch_note: feeds bucket-canon/05-biophysics as ONE partial source, not the centre
disputed: Many causal claims (EMF→disease, cold→longevity) are speculative/unfalsifiable as stated; blog format, not peer-reviewed; mechanism-to-outcome conflation is frequent.

name: Herbert Fröhlich

primary_works.title: Long-range coherence and energy storage in biological systems (Int. J. Quantum Chem.)
Bose condensation of strongly excited longitudinal electric modes

field_contribution: Proposed that biological systems can sustain long-range quantum coherence — 'Fröhlich condensation' — where metabolic energy pumps a macroscopic fraction of molecules into a single coherent vibrational mode, a candidate mechanism for non-thermal collective order in living matter.
why_indexed: A founding theoretical claim of quantum biology; bridges UP to canon-05-biophysics (coherence). Indexed frontier-contested — theoretical tier, experimentally unconfirmed in vivo.
cross_branch_note: bridges UP to bucket-canon/05-biophysics (coherence); sibling to the carded Popp
disputed: In-vivo Fröhlich condensation has never been experimentally demonstrated; remains a theoretical proposal.

name: László Boros

primary_works.title: Submolecular regulation of cell transformation by deuterium (review)
Deuterium depletion and mitochondrial matrix water (stable-isotope tracing)

field_contribution: Argues that the deuterium/hydrogen ratio of metabolic water matters biologically — that mitochondrial nanomotors discriminate against deuterium, and that deuterium load affects cell proliferation and metabolism. Uses stable-isotope-resolved metabolomics (SIRM) as the analytic method.
why_indexed: A primary scientific voice for the deuterium-metabolism thesis that bridges to the biophysics water substrate; indexed frontier-contested.
disputed: Clinical relevance of deuterium depletion in humans is unproven; effect sizes and disease claims are contested.

name: Gábor Somlyai

primary_works.title: Naturally occurring deuterium is essential for the normal growth rate of cells (FEBS Lett)
Deuterium-depleted water in cancer adjunct trials (HYD)

field_contribution: Pioneered deuterium-depleted water (DDW) as a clinical intervention, founding HYD to produce DDW and running studies (mostly observational/small) on DDW as an adjunct in cancer and metabolic conditions. The contribution is operationalizing deuterium depletion into a deliverable product and clinical program.
why_indexed: The clinical translator of the deuterium thesis; indexed clinical-translator with evidence largely at anecdotal/small-trial tier.
disputed: Trials are small, often unblinded, with commercial COI (HYD); DDW efficacy not established by RCT.

name: Andy Galpin
region: Cal State Fullerton / Parker University, USA

primary_works.title: Single-muscle-fiber adaptation to training (primary research)
Unplugged (book, w/ Brian MacKenzie)

field_contribution: Researches human skeletal-muscle physiology at the single-fiber level and translates strength/power/endurance programming, fiber-type adaptation, and recovery for athletes and the public. Champions resistance training and adequate protein for healthspan against the protein-restriction camp.
why_indexed: A rigorous translator of muscle physiology and the strength/protein side of the longevity diet conflict.

name: Stuart McGill

primary_works.title: Low Back Disorders (textbook)
Lumbar spine load tolerance and the 'Big Three' stabilization exercises

field_contribution: Quantified lumbar-spine loading and injury mechanics in the lab, defining spine-sparing movement principles, the role of core stiffness/bracing, and rehabilitation built on the 'McGill Big Three' (curl-up, side bridge, bird-dog) rather than spinal flexion.
why_indexed: The empirical foundation of modern spine biomechanics and evidence-based back-pain management.

name: Kelly Starrett

primary_works.title: Becoming a Supple Leopard (book)
MobilityWOD / The Ready State (platform)

field_contribution: Physical therapist who systematized a popular mobility framework — positional/joint mobilization, tissue work, and movement 'archetypes' for athletes — bringing mobility self-treatment to a mass strength-and-conditioning audience. A practitioner system, evidence largely anecdotal/mechanistic.
why_indexed: The most influential popularizer of mobility-as-practice; indexed practitioner-n1.
disputed: Specific claims (e.g., fascia 'smashing', precise positional cues) often outrun the evidence tier.

name: Pavel Tsatsouline

primary_works.title: The Russian Kettlebell Challenge (book)
Power to the People! / 'grease the groove' methodology

field_contribution: Introduced the Russian kettlebell and 'strength as a skill' methodology to the West — high-tension techniques, sub-failure high-frequency practice ('grease the groove'), and minimalist programming. A practitioner/coach contribution to strength culture, not laboratory science.
why_indexed: Reshaped Western strength practice and popularized the kettlebell as a longevity-relevant tool; indexed practitioner-n1.

name: Ido Portal

primary_works.title: 'Movement Culture' methodology / workshops
Conor McGregor movement-coaching collaboration

field_contribution: Built 'Movement Culture' — a discipline-agnostic practice blending hand-balancing, locomotion, dance, martial and gymnastic elements into general movement capacity, explicitly opposing specialization. A practitioner/teacher tradition transmitted through workshops, not papers.
why_indexed: The signature figure of the general-movement / locomotion revival; indexed practitioner-n1.

name: Stan Efferding

primary_works.title: The Vertical Diet (protocol/book, w/ Damon McCune)
Rhino strength/nutrition coaching content

field_contribution: Powerlifter/bodybuilder coach who created the 'Vertical Diet' — a high-protein, easily-digested, micronutrient-dense practical eating system — and popularized pragmatic performance-nutrition heuristics (meal timing, sodium, blood-pressure management) for strength athletes.
why_indexed: A widely-followed practitioner node for performance nutrition; indexed practitioner-n1, evidence anecdotal.

name: Wim Hof

primary_works.title: The Wim Hof Method (book/program)
Voluntary modulation of the autonomic nervous system / innate immune response (PNAS, Kox et al.)

field_contribution: Developed a method combining cyclic hyperventilation breathing, cold exposure, and focus; subject of the Kox 2014 study showing trained practitioners can voluntarily blunt the inflammatory response to endotoxin — a rare case where a practitioner method generated a controlled mechanistic result.
why_indexed: The central practitioner node linking breath + cold + autonomic control; one method with one notable mechanistic study, otherwise anecdotal.
disputed: Outcome claims far exceed the single small mechanistic study; hyperventilation+water carries real drowning/blackout risk.

name: Patrick McKeown

primary_works.title: The Oxygen Advantage (book)
Buteyko method instruction for asthma/sleep

field_contribution: Leading modern teacher of Buteyko-derived breathing — nasal breathing, reduced-volume breathing to raise CO2 tolerance (BOLT score), and breath-light practices for asthma, sleep, and performance. A practitioner/educator extending Buteyko's framework.
why_indexed: The principal contemporary transmitter of nasal/CO2-tolerance breathing practice; indexed practitioner-n1.

name: James Nestor

primary_works.title: Breath: The New Science of a Lost Art (book)
Stanford nasal-vs-mouth breathing self-experiment (w/ Jayakar Nayak)

field_contribution: Journalist whose book 'Breath' synthesized respiratory physiology, the case for nasal over mouth breathing, slow/coherent breathing (~5.5 breaths/min), and CO2 tolerance for a mass audience, including a documented nasal-obstruction self-experiment with Stanford collaborators.
why_indexed: The dominant popular synthesizer of breath science; indexed communicator — grade the cited primary work.

name: Jari Laukkanen

primary_works.title: Association between sauna bathing and fatal cardiovascular and all-cause mortality (JAMA Intern Med)
Sauna bathing and incident dementia (KIHD cohort)

field_contribution: Led the Finnish KIHD cohort analyses showing frequent sauna use (4–7×/week) is associated with substantially lower cardiovascular and all-cause mortality and lower dementia incidence, establishing the dose-response sauna-longevity association in a large prospective population.
why_indexed: The empirical backbone of the heat-stress / sauna longevity literature.
disputed: Observational; healthy-user bias and reverse causation not fully excluded; no RCT.

name: Susanna Søberg

primary_works.title: Winter swimming and brown-adipose-tissue / cold-heat adaptation (Cell Reports Medicine)
The 'Søberg principle' / thermogenesis protocols

field_contribution: Studied winter swimmers to characterize cold + heat (contrast) effects on brown adipose tissue activation and metabolic health, and translated a practical dosing heuristic (the 'Søberg principle': end on cold, ~11 min/week cold exposure) widely cited in the cold-exposure community.
why_indexed: A primary researcher who also operationalized cold/heat thermogenesis into a citable protocol.

name: Wouter van Marken Lichtenbelt

primary_works.title: Cold-activated brown adipose tissue in healthy men (NEJM)
Non-shivering thermogenesis and thermoneutral-zone / healthy variability work

field_contribution: Co-authored the landmark demonstration that functional brown adipose tissue is present and cold-activatable in adult humans (PET-CT), reopening BAT as a metabolic target, and developed the concept of 'healthy thermal variability' against constant thermoneutral indoor living.
why_indexed: Provided the human evidence that adult brown fat exists and responds to cold — the mechanistic foundation under cold-exposure metabolic claims.

name: Matthew Walker

primary_works.title: Why We Sleep (book)
Sleep and memory consolidation / emotional regulation (primary research)

field_contribution: Sleep neuroscientist whose primary work links sleep (esp. NREM slow-wave and REM) to memory consolidation and emotional regulation, and whose book 'Why We Sleep' brought sleep-health science to a mass audience. Both a researcher and a major communicator.
why_indexed: The dominant popular voice on sleep's role in health and aging; indexed as communicator where the book overstates, rigorous where the lab work stands.
disputed: 'Why We Sleep' contains documented factual overstatements/errors (Guzey critique 2019); grade specific claims individually.

name: Satchin Panda

primary_works.title: Melanopsin (Opn4) as the circadian photopigment (Science)
Time-restricted feeding prevents metabolic disease in mice (Cell Metab)

field_contribution: Helped identify melanopsin as the non-visual photoreceptor that entrains the circadian clock to light, then showed that time-restricted feeding (eating within a confined daily window) protects mice from diet-induced metabolic disease independent of calories — founding the time-restricted-eating field.
why_indexed: Connects the light-entrainment substrate to a concrete metabolic intervention (TRE); a key circadian-to-metabolism node.

name: Maiken Nedergaard

primary_works.title: A paravascular pathway facilitates CSF flow and clearance — the glymphatic system (Sci Transl Med)
Sleep drives metabolite clearance from the adult brain (Science)

field_contribution: Discovered the glymphatic system — a glia-dependent perivascular network that clears metabolic waste (including amyloid-beta) from the brain — and showed it is markedly more active during sleep, providing a mechanistic link between sleep and neurodegeneration risk.
why_indexed: Gave sleep a concrete brain-clearance mechanism, central to sleep-aging-dementia claims.
disputed: Magnitude and some mechanics of glymphatic flow (and anesthesia effects) are debated in the literature.

name: David M. Sabatini

primary_works.title: Discovery of mTOR (mammalian target of rapamycin) (Cell)
mTORC1 senses amino acids via the Rag GTPases / Sestrin / lysosome

field_contribution: Co-discovered mTOR and then mapped how mTORC1 senses nutrients — amino acids via Rag GTPases at the lysosome, the Sestrin leucine sensor — defining the central nutrient-sensing pathway whose inhibition (rapamycin, fasting, protein restriction) underlies most longevity interventions.
why_indexed: mTOR is the molecular hub of the nutrient-sensing hallmark; Sabatini defined its mechanism. Indexed for the science (note: 2021 misconduct findings ended his MIT post — a personnel matter, separate from the validity of the mTOR biology).
disputed: 2021 institutional misconduct findings (sexual-harassment) cost him his positions; does not bear on the mTOR science itself.
surfaced_via: Kaeberlein, Longo, Kennedy cards (mTOR appears in many)

name: Michael N. Hall

primary_works.title: TOR1/TOR2 identified in yeast as targets of rapamycin (Cell)
TOR as a central controller of cell growth (reviews)

field_contribution: Discovered the TOR genes in yeast (1991) as the molecular targets of rapamycin, establishing TOR as the conserved master regulator of cell growth in response to nutrients — the discovery that mTOR/Sabatini work later extended to mammals. Lasker Award 2017.
why_indexed: Original discovery of the TOR pathway, the most-targeted longevity node; the yeast foundation under all mTOR geroscience.
surfaced_via: Sabatini/Kaeberlein cards — TOR origin appears repeatedly

name: Leonard Guarente

primary_works.title: SIR2 extends replicative lifespan in yeast (Cell/Genes Dev)
Sir2/NAD+ links metabolism to aging and caloric restriction

field_contribution: Showed that the SIR2 gene (a NAD+-dependent deacetylase) regulates replicative lifespan in yeast and links caloric restriction to longevity through NAD+, founding the sirtuin field of aging research. Mentor to David Sinclair.
why_indexed: Originated the sirtuin/NAD+ theory of aging — one of the two or three dominant molecular frameworks in the field.
disputed: Some sirtuin lifespan claims (incl. resveratrol activation) were later challenged; the core NAD+/Sir2 biology stands.
surfaced_via: Sinclair, Verdin, Imai cards — sirtuin origin

name: Elizabeth Blackburn

primary_works.title: Discovery of telomerase (w/ Carol Greider) (Cell)
The Telomere Effect (book, w/ Elissa Epel)

field_contribution: Co-discovered telomerase, the enzyme that extends telomeres (chromosome-end caps), and characterized telomere structure — establishing telomere attrition as a hallmark of aging and a link between cellular replication limits and organismal aging. Nobel Prize 2009.
why_indexed: Telomere attrition is a canonical hallmark of aging; Blackburn discovered the enzyme that governs it.
disputed: Telomere-length-as-biomarker and psychosocial-stress→telomere claims (Telomere Effect) are weaker than the core enzymology.

name: Carol W. Greider
region: UC Santa Cruz / formerly Johns Hopkins, USA

primary_works.title: Identification of telomerase activity (w/ Blackburn) (Cell)
Telomere shortening and cellular senescence (mouse knockout models)

field_contribution: As a graduate student co-discovered telomerase activity, then characterized telomerase-knockout mice showing progressive telomere shortening causes tissue failure and premature-aging phenotypes, cementing telomere maintenance as causal in aging and cancer. Nobel Prize 2009.
why_indexed: Provided the mechanistic and genetic proof that telomere maintenance governs replicative aging.

name: Linda Partridge
region: UCL / Max Planck Institute for Biology of Ageing, UK/Germany

primary_works.title: Hallmarks of Aging co-author (Cell)
Dietary restriction, insulin/IGF and TOR in Drosophila longevity

field_contribution: A leading experimental gerontologist who dissected how dietary restriction, insulin/IGF signalling, and TOR extend lifespan in flies and mice (including which dietary components — not just calories — matter), and co-authored the Hallmarks of Aging.
why_indexed: Bridged evolutionary theory and experimental nutrient-sensing biology of aging across model organisms; a Hallmarks architect.

name: Brian K. Kennedy
region: National University of Singapore; formerly Buck Institute, USA/Singapore

primary_works.title: Geroscience: Linking Aging to Chronic Disease (Cell, lead author)
SIR2 / replicative aging mechanisms (w/ Guarente, early career)

field_contribution: Helped define 'geroscience' — the thesis that targeting aging biology can simultaneously delay multiple chronic diseases — as a field and policy frame, and ran the Buck Institute. Works on mTOR/rapamycin and translation of geroprotectors.
why_indexed: A principal architect of the geroscience hypothesis that organizes the whole field's translational rationale.

name: James L. Kirkland

primary_works.title: The Achilles' heel of senescent cells: senolytics (dasatinib+quercetin) (Aging Cell)
First-in-human senolytic trials (IPF, diabetic kidney disease)

field_contribution: Co-introduced senolytics — drugs (dasatinib + quercetin, fisetin) that selectively kill senescent cells — demonstrated healthspan extension in mice, and led the first-in-human senolytic trials, turning Campisi's senescence biology into a therapeutic strategy.
why_indexed: Translated the senescence hallmark into the first clinical senolytic interventions.

name: Steven Austad
region: University of Alabama at Birmingham, USA

primary_works.title: Retarded senescence in an insular opossum population (J. Zoology)
Why We Age (book)

field_contribution: Tested evolutionary theories of aging in the wild (island opossums with relaxed predation evolve slower aging), championed long-lived species (naked mole-rats, bats, clams) as windows into aging mechanisms, and famously bet (with Olshansky) on human lifespan limits.
why_indexed: A founder of comparative biogerontology — using species that defy the aging 'rules' to find what governs lifespan.

name: Richard A. Miller

primary_works.title: Rapamycin fed late in life extends lifespan in genetically heterogeneous mice (Nature, ITP)
NIA Interventions Testing Program (ITP) design & results

field_contribution: Co-leads the NIA Interventions Testing Program (ITP), the rigorous multi-site replicated mouse-lifespan testing platform that produced the landmark finding that rapamycin extends lifespan even when started in old age, and validated/refuted many candidate geroprotectors (acarbose, 17-α-estradiol vs. resveratrol).
why_indexed: Built the gold-standard replicated testbed that separates real geroprotectors from hype — the field's quality filter.

name: Thomas Rando
region: UCLA (Broad Stem Cell); formerly Stanford, USA

primary_works.title: Rejuvenation of aged muscle stem cells via Notch (w/ Conboy) (Nature/Science)
Quiescence and the aging stem-cell niche

field_contribution: Showed that aged muscle satellite (stem) cells lose regenerative capacity largely because of the systemic and niche environment (Notch signalling), not irreversible intrinsic damage — a foundational parabiosis/stem-cell-aging result with the Conboys.
why_indexed: Established that stem-cell aging is substantially environmental and reversible — a pillar of regenerative geroscience.

name: Amy Wagers

primary_works.title: GDF11 as a circulating 'rejuvenating' factor in heart and muscle (Cell/Science)
Parabiosis and blood-borne factors in tissue aging

field_contribution: Used parabiosis to search for specific blood-borne youthful factors, proposing GDF11 as a circulating factor whose age-related decline drives cardiac hypertrophy and muscle/brain aging — a high-profile 'rejuvenation factor' claim.
why_indexed: A central figure in the young-blood-factor program; indexed frontier-contested due to the GDF11 dispute.
disputed: GDF11 rejuvenation claims were directly contradicted by other labs (Novartis) over antibody specificity and direction of effect; remains unresolved.

name: Saul Villeda

primary_works.title: The ageing systemic milieu negatively regulates neurogenesis and cognition (Nature)
Young blood / exercise factors restore old brain function

field_contribution: Showed that the aged systemic environment suppresses hippocampal neurogenesis and that young blood (and exercise-induced factors like Gpld1, plasma) can restore aspects of cognitive and brain function in old mice — extending parabiosis rejuvenation specifically to the brain.
why_indexed: A key node linking systemic blood factors, exercise, and brain aging/cognition.

name: Eric Topol

primary_works.title: Deep Medicine (book)
Super Agers / the Wellderly genomics and healthy-aging work

field_contribution: Cardiologist and translational researcher applying genomics, AI, and deep phenotyping to medicine, including the 'Wellderly' study of healthy aging and a high-profile synthesis of evidence-based healthy-longevity practice (lifestyle, immune aging, screening) for the public.
why_indexed: A rigorous, high-visibility translator connecting biomarkers/AI/genomics to healthy aging.

name: Luigi Fontana
region: University of Sydney; formerly Washington Univ. St. Louis, Italy/Australia

primary_works.title: Long-term calorie restriction in humans: metabolic & cardiovascular effects (PNAS)
Promoting health and longevity through diet (Cell review)

field_contribution: Led the human caloric-restriction studies (CRONies cohort, then CALERIE-related work) showing long-term CR lowers cardiometabolic risk, IGF-1, inflammation, and core temperature in people — translating rodent CR biology to controlled human data, while clarifying protein's role.
why_indexed: Provided the principal human evidence base for caloric/dietary restriction effects on aging biomarkers.

name: Mark Mattson

primary_works.title: Intermittent metabolic switching, neuroplasticity and brain health (review)
Effects of Intermittent Fasting on Health, Aging, and Disease (NEJM)

field_contribution: Pioneered the neuroscience of intermittent fasting and hormesis — that intermittent energetic stress (fasting, exercise) triggers adaptive, protective responses (BDNF, ketones, autophagy, mitochondrial biogenesis) that benefit the brain and slow aging ('intermittent metabolic switching').
why_indexed: A founder of the fasting/hormesis-for-brain-aging framework, grounding it in adaptive-stress neurobiology.

name: Charles Brenner

primary_works.title: Discovery of nicotinamide riboside (NR) as an NAD+ precursor vitamin (Cell)
Quantitative NAD+ metabolomics / NRK pathway

field_contribution: Discovered nicotinamide riboside (NR) and the NRK kinase pathway as a route to boost NAD+, and is the field's leading rigorous voice on what NAD+ metabolism actually does — and a prominent skeptic correcting overstated NMN/NAD+ anti-aging and 'reverse aging' claims.
why_indexed: Defines the real biochemistry of NAD+ precursors and serves as the empirical check on NAD+ hype (the Sinclair counterweight).
disputed: Publicly disputes Sinclair-style NMN/longevity claims; commercial NR ties (ChromaDex) are a COI to note.

name: Shin-ichiro Imai
region: Washington University in St. Louis, USA

primary_works.title: Transcriptional silencing and longevity by Sir2 as an NAD-dependent deacetylase (Nature, w/ Guarente)
NMN improves age-associated physiological decline in mice (Cell Metab)

field_contribution: Co-showed that Sir2 is an NAD+-dependent deacetylase (linking metabolism to the epigenome), proposed the 'NAD World' systemic aging framework centered on the NAD+-synthesizing enzyme NAMPT, and produced the mouse data motivating NMN supplementation.
why_indexed: A principal architect of the NAD+/NMN theory of systemic aging; indexed frontier-contested pending human efficacy data.
disputed: NMN human benefits unproven; 'NAD World' is a framework, not established; commercial NMN interest is a COI.

name: Rafael de Cabo

primary_works.title: Caloric restriction improves health and survival of rhesus monkeys (Nature Comm, NIA)
Effects of fasting/meal timing independent of calories in mice (Cell Metab)

field_contribution: Ran the NIA rhesus-monkey caloric-restriction study and helped reconcile it with the divergent Wisconsin result (diet composition and feeding controls explain the difference), and showed that fasting interval/meal timing improves rodent healthspan independent of calorie or diet content.
why_indexed: Provided the primate-level CR evidence and disentangled calories from timing — key to interpreting the human CR/TRE literature.

name: Gary Ruvkun

primary_works.title: daf-2 encodes an insulin-receptor-like protein controlling C. elegans lifespan (Science/Nature)
Discovery of the let-7 microRNA and heterochronic gene control (Nature)

field_contribution: Identified daf-2 as an insulin/IGF-1-receptor homolog and the DAF-16/FOXO pathway controlling worm lifespan (with Kenyon's phenotype), and separately co-discovered microRNAs (let-7) — establishing the molecular wiring of the insulin/IGF longevity pathway. Nobel Prize 2024 (miRNA).
why_indexed: Defined the molecular identity of the insulin/IGF-1 longevity pathway, conserved from worms to humans.

name: Andrzej Bartke

primary_works.title: Extending the lifespan of long-lived mice: GH-deficient Ames/Snell dwarfs (Nature)
Growth-hormone-resistant (GHR-KO) Laron mice hold the mouse longevity record

field_contribution: Showed that growth-hormone-deficient (Ames, Snell) and GH-resistant (Laron) dwarf mice live dramatically longer than normal mice — the strongest single-gene mammalian longevity effect — establishing that reduced GH/IGF-1 signalling extends mammalian lifespan, mirroring human Laron-syndrome cancer/diabetes protection.
why_indexed: The mammalian proof that the GH/IGF-1 axis sets lifespan, anchoring the protein/IGF-1 longevity debate in mouse genetics.

name: Thomas Kirkwood

primary_works.title: Evolution of ageing — the disposable soma theory (Nature)
Time of Our Lives (book)

field_contribution: Proposed the 'disposable soma' theory — organisms allocate limited energy between reproduction and somatic maintenance, so aging results from evolutionarily optimal under-investment in repair — providing the dominant evolutionary explanation for why aging exists and why nutrient-sensing/repair pathways govern it.
why_indexed: The reigning evolutionary-theory foundation that explains *why* the cellular hallmarks of aging are tolerated.

name: Denham Harman

primary_works.title: Aging: a theory based on free radical and radiation chemistry (J. Gerontol)
The biologic clock: the mitochondria? (mitochondrial free-radical theory)

field_contribution: Proposed the free-radical theory of aging (1956) and its mitochondrial variant (1972) — that accumulated oxidative damage from reactive oxygen species drives aging — the single most influential mechanistic aging theory of the 20th century and the rationale for the entire antioxidant field.
why_indexed: The foundational oxidative-damage theory of aging; indexed frontier-contested because the simple version is now substantially revised.
disputed: Antioxidant supplementation largely failed to extend lifespan; ROS now seen as also adaptive (mitohormesis); the simple 'oxidative damage = aging' version is considered insufficient.
surfaced_via: Harman is cited as origin in nearly every aging-mechanism source

name: Leonard Hayflick

primary_works.title: The serial cultivation of human diploid cell strains — the Hayflick limit (Exp Cell Res)
The limited in vitro lifetime of human diploid cell strains

field_contribution: Demonstrated that normal human cells divide only a finite number of times in culture (the 'Hayflick limit') before entering senescence, overturning the dogma of cellular immortality and founding the concept of replicative senescence — later mechanistically tied to telomere shortening.
why_indexed: Established replicative senescence as a real, intrinsic cellular aging clock — the empirical bedrock under the senescence hallmark.

name: Roy Walford

primary_works.title: The Retardation of Aging and Disease by Dietary Restriction (book)
Caloric restriction during Biosphere 2 closure (PNAS)

field_contribution: A leading 20th-century caloric-restriction researcher who advanced the immunologic theory of aging and famously practiced and documented severe CR himself, including during the Biosphere 2 enclosure — bringing rodent CR longevity findings toward human self-experiment and public attention.
why_indexed: A pivotal bridge figure carrying caloric restriction from rodent labs toward human practice; indexed frontier-contested (his own severe-CR advocacy outran the human evidence).
disputed: Severe-CR human longevity benefit never demonstrated; Walford himself died at 79 of ALS; Biosphere CR was confounded.

name: Clive McCay

primary_works.title: The effect of retarded growth upon the length of life span (J. Nutrition)
Retarded growth, lifespan, and ultimate body size in rats

field_contribution: Performed the original caloric-restriction experiments (1935) showing that rats fed a calorie-restricted but nutritionally adequate diet lived substantially longer than freely-fed rats — the first demonstration that diet can extend maximum lifespan, founding the entire field of dietary longevity intervention.
why_indexed: The origin experiment of caloric restriction — the most robust, most-replicated longevity intervention in biology.

name: Hans Selye

primary_works.title: A syndrome produced by diverse nocuous agents — the General Adaptation Syndrome (Nature)
The Stress of Life (book)

field_contribution: Defined biological 'stress' and the General Adaptation Syndrome (alarm → resistance → exhaustion), and distinguished beneficial 'eustress' from harmful distress — the conceptual foundation under hormesis, allostatic load, and the entire stress-physiology basis of cold/heat/exercise adaptation.
why_indexed: Originated the scientific concept of physiological stress and adaptation that underlies all hormesis and recovery science.

name: Ancel Keys

primary_works.title: The Seven Countries Study (diet, lifestyle, cardiovascular disease)
The Biology of Human Starvation (Minnesota Starvation Experiment)

field_contribution: Ran the Seven Countries Study linking saturated-fat intake and serum cholesterol to cardiovascular disease (the diet-heart hypothesis), conducted the Minnesota Starvation Experiment, and developed the K-ration and Body Mass Index usage — shaping 20th-century diet-disease epidemiology.
why_indexed: The origin of the diet-heart hypothesis that still structures nutrition debates; indexed frontier-contested because the saturated-fat conclusions remain disputed (the central nutrition conflict).
disputed: Seven Countries country-selection and the saturated-fat conclusions are heavily contested (Teicholz et al.); a live, unresolved nutrition conflict.
surfaced_via: nutrition-conflict thread (seed oils / saturated fat in the map)

name: Kenneth H. Cooper

primary_works.title: Aerobics (book)
Cooper Center Longitudinal Study — fitness and mortality

field_contribution: Coined 'aerobics,' created the 12-minute and 1.5-mile fitness tests, and built the Cooper Center Longitudinal Study whose data established cardiorespiratory fitness (VO2max-proxy) as a powerful independent predictor of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality.
why_indexed: Founded the quantification of aerobic fitness and the cohort evidence that cardiorespiratory fitness is among the strongest longevity predictors.

name: Iñigo San Millán
region: University of Colorado / Univ. of Texat Austin, USA (Spanish)

primary_works.title: Metabolic flexibility, lactate clearance and mitochondrial function in athletes/metabolic disease
Zone-2 training and the lactate threshold (applied physiology)

field_contribution: Popularized and clinically framed 'Zone 2' training — exercise at the intensity that maximizes fat oxidation and mitochondrial function just below lactate accumulation — as a longevity and metabolic-health lever, linking lactate-clearance capacity to mitochondrial health and insulin sensitivity.
why_indexed: The principal translator of mitochondrial/lactate exercise physiology into the widely-adopted Zone-2 longevity protocol.

name: Stuart Phillips

primary_works.title: Mixed muscle protein synthesis after resistance exercise and protein feeding (Am J Physiol)
Protein 'requirements' beyond the RDA for muscle and aging (reviews)

field_contribution: Quantified how resistance exercise and dietary protein (leucine, dose, distribution, timing) drive muscle protein synthesis, building the evidence that higher-than-RDA protein and resistance training protect against sarcopenia — the empirical core of the strength/protein side of the longevity diet conflict.
why_indexed: The primary muscle-protein-synthesis evidence base; the rigorous counterweight to protein-restriction longevity claims.
disputed: Higher-protein-for-longevity stance opposes the Longo/IGF-1 restriction camp; likely age/context dependent.

name: Brad Schoenfeld

primary_works.title: The mechanisms of muscle hypertrophy and their application to resistance training (J Strength Cond Res)
Dose-response of training volume and frequency for hypertrophy (meta-analyses)

field_contribution: Systematized the science of skeletal-muscle hypertrophy — mechanical tension as the primary driver, training-volume dose-response, the relative unimportance of rep-range vs. effort/proximity-to-failure — via primary trials and meta-analyses, replacing bodybuilding lore with evidence.
why_indexed: The reference evidence base for how resistance training builds muscle, the tissue most protective against frailty mortality.

name: Tim Spector

primary_works.title: TwinsUK registry (founder)
PREDICT studies of personalized postprandial responses; ZOE (Spoon-Fed book)

field_contribution: Founded TwinsUK (a major heritability/epigenetics cohort), then led the PREDICT studies showing large person-to-person variation in metabolic responses to identical foods, and championed gut-microbiome diversity and dietary-fiber/plant variety ('30 plants a week') as health levers, commercialized via ZOE.
why_indexed: A primary node linking the microbiome and personalized-nutrition response to metabolic health and aging.
disputed: ZOE commercial COI; individualized-response claims are strong but their longevity payoff is unproven.
surfaced_via: microbiome thread (gut-everything axis in the map)

name: Eran Segal

primary_works.title: Personalized nutrition by prediction of glycemic responses (Cell)
PREDICT postprandial-response studies (w/ Spector)

field_contribution: Showed (via continuous glucose monitoring + microbiome + a machine-learning model) that postprandial glucose responses to identical meals vary enormously between people and can be predicted and personalized — founding data-driven personalized nutrition and validating CGM-guided N=1 dietary tailoring.
why_indexed: Provided the rigorous proof-of-concept for personalized, measurement-driven nutrition — the data backbone under CGM biohacking.

name: Konstantin Buteyko

primary_works.title: The Buteyko breathing method (clinical practice, USSR)
Reduced-breathing / CO2-tolerance theory of disease

field_contribution: A Soviet physician who developed the Buteyko method — deliberate reduced-volume, nasal breathing to raise arterial CO2 tolerance — claiming chronic over-breathing (hyperventilation) underlies asthma and many disorders. The method's asthma-symptom benefit has modest RCT support; its broader disease theory does not.
why_indexed: The origin of the modern CO2-tolerance / nasal-breathing breathwork lineage that McKeown and Nestor transmit.
disputed: Asthma symptom/medication-reduction has some RCT support; the broad 'hyperventilation causes most disease' theory is not validated.

name: B. K. S. Iyengar

primary_works.title: Light on Yoga (book)
Light on Pranayama (book)

field_contribution: Systematized Hatha yoga asana into a precise, alignment-based, prop-assisted method (Iyengar Yoga), codifying hundreds of postures with detailed technique in 'Light on Yoga' — the most influential transmission of yoga asana to the modern world and the basis for most clinical yoga research.
why_indexed: The principal codifier of modern postural yoga, the movement/flexibility tradition most studied for measurable health effects.

name: Joseph Pilates

primary_works.title: Your Health (book)
Return to Life Through Contrology (book)

field_contribution: Created 'Contrology' (now Pilates) — a mat- and apparatus-based system emphasizing core control, alignment, breath, and controlled whole-body movement — that became a foundational modern method for core stability, rehabilitation, and mobility.
why_indexed: Originated one of the two or three dominant Western movement/core-conditioning systems still in clinical and fitness use.

name: Moshe Feldenkrais

primary_works.title: Awareness Through Movement (book)
The Potent Self / Body and Mature Behaviour

field_contribution: A physicist and judoka who created the Feldenkrais Method — slow, attention-based movement sequences that use the nervous system's capacity to relearn movement patterns to improve mobility, reduce pain, and reorganize motor control ('awareness through movement', 'functional integration').
why_indexed: A founding somatic-education method linking movement, attention, and neuroplasticity — distinct from strength/stretch paradigms.
surfaced_via: movement library (map domain F) + somatic lineage

name: Thomas Myers

primary_works.title: Anatomy Trains: Myofascial Meridians (book)

field_contribution: Proposed 'Anatomy Trains' — that muscles are functionally linked into continuous myofascial 'meridian' lines transmitting tension across the body — reframing movement and bodywork around fascial continuity rather than isolated muscles. A practitioner framework with partial anatomical support.
why_indexed: The dominant popular framework for fascia/myofascial-chain thinking in movement and manual therapy; indexed practitioner-n1.
disputed: Specific 'meridian line' continuity and force-transmission claims are only partly supported by dissection/biomechanics evidence.

name: Coleen Murphy

primary_works.title: Genes that act downstream of DAF-16 to influence C. elegans lifespan (Nature, w/ Kenyon)
Reproductive and cognitive aging / transgenerational memory in C. elegans

field_contribution: Identified the genome-wide set of DAF-16/FOXO target genes that mediate insulin/IGF lifespan extension in C. elegans, and extended worm-aging genetics to reproductive aging and learning/memory decline — connecting the canonical longevity pathway to functional healthspan.
why_indexed: Mapped the effector genes downstream of the field's founding longevity pathway and broadened it to cognitive/reproductive aging.

name: Dudley Lamming

primary_works.title: Rapamycin-induced insulin resistance is mediated by mTORC2 loss (Science)
Restriction of dietary branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs) improves metabolic health (mouse)

field_contribution: Dissected how rapamycin's benefits (mTORC1) separate from its side effects (mTORC2/insulin resistance), and showed that restricting specific dietary amino acids (branched-chain amino acids, especially isoleucine) — not just total protein — improves metabolic health and extends lifespan in mice, refining the protein-longevity debate.
why_indexed: Moved the protein/mTOR longevity question from 'how much protein' to 'which amino acids,' and clarified rapamycin's dual signalling.

name: Gilbert Ling
note: association-induction hypothesis, cell water — already carded

name: Nick Lane

primary_works.title: Power, Sex, Suicide: Mitochondria and the Meaning of Life
The Vital Question: Energy, Evolution, and the Origins of Complex Life

field_contribution: Synthesized the case that membrane-bound proton gradients (chemiosmosis) set the energetic constraints on the origin of life and the leap to eukaryotic complexity, arguing that mitochondrial bioenergetics, not genes alone, gate the size and complexity a cell can reach. The bridge author connecting mainstream mitochondrial biology to deep bioenergetic theory.
why_indexed: The principal contemporary synthesizer linking chemiosmotic theory, endosymbiosis, and origin-of-life to mitochondrial aging; the readable spine under the corpus's bioenergetics vertical.

name: Peter D. Mitchell

primary_works.title: Coupling of phosphorylation to electron and hydrogen transfer by a chemi-osmotic type of mechanism (Nature)
Chemiosmotic Coupling in Oxidative and Photosynthetic Phosphorylation

field_contribution: Proposed and defended chemiosmotic theory: ATP synthesis is powered by a transmembrane electrochemical proton gradient (the proton-motive force) generated by the respiratory chain, not by a chemical high-energy intermediate. Won the 1978 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for the theory.
why_indexed: Chemiosmosis is the actual physical law under mitochondrial ATP production: canon-tier (05-biophysics), the foundation beneath every downstream mitochondrial-aging claim.
disputed: Chemiosmotic theory was fiercely resisted for ~15 years (the 'ox-phos wars') before experimental validation.

name: Jennifer Moyle

primary_works.title: Estimation of membrane potential and pH difference across mitochondrial membranes (with Mitchell)
Proton translocation experiments establishing H+/O ratios

field_contribution: Co-developed and experimentally proved chemiosmosis alongside Mitchell, providing the quantitative proton-translocation measurements (H+/O and H+/ATP stoichiometries) that turned the theory from proposal into validated mechanism.
why_indexed: The experimental half of the chemiosmotic proof; indexed both for the science and as a documented case of an under-credited collaborator.
disputed: Substantially under-credited relative to Mitchell despite co-authoring the decisive experimental papers; not included in the 1978 Nobel.

name: Lynn Margulis

primary_works.title: On the Origin of Mitosing Cells (J. Theoretical Biology, as Lynn Sagan)
Symbiosis in Cell Evolution

field_contribution: Revived and established serial endosymbiotic theory: mitochondria and chloroplasts originated as free-living bacteria taken up by host cells, making organelles the descendants of ancient symbionts. Upstream of every mitochondrial-origin and mitochondrial-aging argument.
why_indexed: The endosymbiotic origin of mitochondria is the biological foundation under all bioenergetic-aging claims; canon-adjacent (origin of complexity).
disputed: Also championed the Gaia hypothesis and broader symbiogenesis-drives-speciation claims that remain contested.

name: William F. (Bill) Martin

primary_works.title: The hydrogen hypothesis for the first eukaryote (Nature, with Muller)
On the origin of biochemistry at an alkaline hydrothermal vent (with Russell)

field_contribution: Proposed the hydrogen hypothesis for eukaryogenesis and, with Michael Russell, the alkaline-hydrothermal-vent theory in which natural proton gradients across mineral membranes drive the first metabolism, grounding the origin of life in chemiosmotic geochemistry. Nick Lane's principal scientific collaborator.
why_indexed: Carries chemiosmosis back to the origin of life itself; the origin-of-life foundation under the corpus's bioenergetics thread.

name: Carl Woese
region: University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, USA

primary_works.title: Phylogenetic structure of the prokaryotic domain: the primary kingdoms (PNAS)
Towards a natural system of organisms: proposal for the domains Archaea, Bacteria, and Eucarya (PNAS)

field_contribution: Defined the Archaea as a third domain of life through 16S ribosomal-RNA phylogenetics, reorganizing the tree of life and founding molecular phylogenetics as a method. Established rRNA as the universal molecular clock for deep evolutionary relationships.
why_indexed: The three-domains tree is the information-theoretic backbone of how life is classified; canon-adjacent (information / biology foundation).

name: Hans Adolf Krebs

primary_works.title: The citric acid cycle (Enzymologia)
Untersuchungen uber die Harnstoffbildung: the urea cycle (with Henseleit)

field_contribution: Discovered the citric-acid (Krebs/TCA) cycle, the central hub of aerobic energy metabolism that oxidizes acetyl-CoA and feeds reducing equivalents to the respiratory chain, and earlier the urea cycle. Won the 1953 Nobel Prize in Medicine.
why_indexed: The TCA cycle is a central metabolic law: the input side of the chemiosmotic machine; foundational to bioenergetics and nutrition alike.

name: Joris Deelen
region: Max Planck Institute for Biology of Ageing (Cologne) / Leiden UMC

primary_works.title: A meta-analysis of genome-wide association studies identifies multiple longevity genes (Nature Communications)
A metabolic profile of all-cause mortality risk (Nature Communications)

field_contribution: Led the largest longevity meta-GWAS, confirming APOE and the 5q33.3/CDKN2B-AS locus as the reproducible human longevity signals, and built metabolomic mortality-risk scores. A consistent voice on the reproducibility limits of longevity GWAS.
why_indexed: Anchors what human genetics actually supports about lifespan: the empirical check on overstated longevity-gene claims.

name: Paola Sebastiani

primary_works.title: Genetic signatures of exceptional longevity in humans (Science, retracted/corrected)
Genetic signatures of exceptional longevity in humans (PLoS ONE, corrected)

field_contribution: Built statistical models of centenarian genetic signatures predicting exceptional longevity. The 2010 Science paper was retracted over genotyping-array artifacts and republished after re-analysis in 2012, a textbook reproducibility object lesson.
why_indexed: Indexed for centenarian-genetics modeling and as a documented case of how genotyping-platform error produces false signals.
disputed: 2010 Science paper retracted for genotyping-chip batch artifacts; corrected version published in PLoS ONE 2012.

name: Thomas Perls

primary_works.title: New England Centenarian Study (founded)
Life-long sustained mortality advantage of siblings of centenarians (PNAS)

field_contribution: Directs the New England Centenarian Study, the largest study of exceptional human longevity, phenotyping centenarians and their families and documenting familial clustering of long life. Also a public debunker of unverified supercentenarian and longevity-product claims.
why_indexed: The phenotyping backbone of human exceptional-longevity research and a quality-control voice against longevity hype.

name: Aleksandra Trifunovic

primary_works.title: Premature ageing in mice expressing defective mitochondrial DNA polymerase (Nature)

field_contribution: Created the POLG 'mutator' mouse: a proofreading-deficient mtDNA polymerase that accumulates mtDNA mutations and produces a premature-aging phenotype, providing direct in-vivo evidence linking mtDNA mutation load to aging.
why_indexed: The mutator mouse is the foundational causal test of the mitochondrial theory of aging.

name: Nils-Goran Larsson

primary_works.title: Premature ageing in mice expressing defective mtDNA polymerase (Nature, senior author)
Mitochondrial transcription factor A (TFAM) and mtDNA maintenance

field_contribution: Senior author of the mtDNA mutator mouse and a principal investigator of mtDNA maintenance biology (TFAM, replication, transcription), establishing the molecular machinery whose failure links mtDNA integrity to aging.
why_indexed: Defined the in-vivo molecular link between mtDNA maintenance and mammalian aging.
surfaced_via: Wave 1 Domain C (mutator mouse senior author)

name: Tomas Prolla

primary_works.title: Mitochondrial DNA mutations, oxidative stress, and apoptosis in mammalian aging (Science, Kujoth et al.)

field_contribution: Produced an independent mutator-mouse line showing that accumulated mtDNA point mutations drive apoptosis-mediated tissue loss and aging, and argued the damage is mutational rather than primarily ROS-driven, refining the oxidative theory.
why_indexed: Independent confirmation that mtDNA mutations cause aging, and an early correction to a purely ROS-centric account.

name: Ake T. Lu
region: Altos Labs (formerly UCLA, Horvath lab), USA

primary_works.title: DNA methylation GrimAge strongly predicts lifespan and healthspan (Aging)
Universal DNA methylation age across mammalian tissues (Nature Aging)

field_contribution: Lead analyst on GrimAge, a second-generation mortality-predictive epigenetic clock, and on the universal pan-mammalian methylation clock, extending clock methodology across species.
why_indexed: Built two of the most-used epigenetic-clock instruments in the field.

name: Albert Higgins-Chen

primary_works.title: A computational solution for bolstering reliability of epigenetic clocks: principal-component clocks (Nature Aging)

field_contribution: Developed principal-component epigenetic clocks that strip technical measurement noise from DNAm age estimates, substantially improving test-retest reliability, a core methodological fix for the clock field's validity problem.
why_indexed: A central validity voice: showed many published epigenetic clocks were unreliable at the individual level and provided the statistical remedy.

name: Daniel Belsky

primary_works.title: Quantification of the pace of biological aging in humans through a blood test: DunedinPACE (eLife)
Change in the rate of biological aging in response to caloric restriction: CALERIE (Nature Aging)

field_contribution: Built the Dunedin pace-of-aging epigenetic measures (DunedinPoAm, DunedinPACE), trained on longitudinal physiological decline rather than chronological age, and applied them to the CALERIE caloric-restriction trial to show measurable slowing of aging pace.
why_indexed: Reframed aging biomarkers from 'how old' to 'how fast you are aging' and tied them to a randomized human intervention.

name: Benoit Lehallier

primary_works.title: Undulating changes in human plasma proteome profiles across the lifespan (Nature Medicine)

field_contribution: Showed the human plasma proteome changes in non-linear 'waves' across the lifespan (clustering near ages ~34, 60, 78) and built a proteomic aging clock from circulating proteins.
why_indexed: Established crests of proteomic aging and the plasma-proteome clock, a foundation of organ/blood-based aging measurement.

name: Hamilton Oh

primary_works.title: Organ aging signatures in the plasma proteome track health and disease (Nature)

field_contribution: Built organ-specific plasma proteomic aging clocks showing that different organs age at different rates within the same person and that an 'aged' organ predicts disease and mortality risk for that system.
why_indexed: Operationalized organ-specific biological age from a single blood draw, a frontier of personalized aging measurement.
surfaced_via: Wave 1 Domain C (organ aging clocks Nature 2023)

name: Michael P. Snyder

primary_works.title: Personal omics profiling reveals dynamic molecular and medical phenotypes: iPOP (Cell)

name: Mahdi Moqri

primary_works.title: Biomarkers of aging for the identification and evaluation of longevity interventions (Cell)

name: Tomasz Wilmanski

primary_works.title: Gut microbiome pattern reflects healthy ageing and predicts survival in humans (Nature Metabolism)

field_contribution: Showed that gut-microbiome compositional uniqueness increases across healthy aging and that this individualized 'drift' predicts survival, linking the microbiome to the aging trajectory.

name: Sean Gibbons

primary_works.title: Gut microbiome pattern reflects healthy ageing and predicts survival in humans (Nature Metabolism, senior author)

field_contribution: Senior author on the microbiome-uniqueness survival work and a principal investigator of systems-level ecological modeling of the gut microbiome and its dynamics in aging and metabolic health.

name: Kenya Honda

primary_works.title: Treg induction by a rationally selected mixture of Clostridia strains (Nature)
An anaerobic bacterial consortium that produces isoalloLCA in centenarians (Nature)

field_contribution: Mapped how specific commensal bacteria induce regulatory T cells (immune tolerance) and identified centenarian gut consortia that produce unusual antimicrobial bile acids (isoalloLCA), linking the microbiome to immune regulation and exceptional longevity.
